title: Responsive Images with srcset, sizes, and picture
summary: Let the browser choose an image that fits the screen and layout.
nestedConcepts: Describe the rendered width with sizes
Balance image quality and transfer size

subtopics.title: Offer image candidates with srcset
subtopics.explanation: `srcset` lists alternate image files and their widths or pixel densities. The browser can choose a suitable file for the screen and layout. For example, provide a small thumbnail and a larger source so a narrow phone does not need to download the full desktop image.

subtopics.title: Describe the rendered width with sizes
subtopics.explanation: `sizes` tells the browser how wide an image will appear at different viewport sizes, before layout finishes. It helps the browser choose an appropriate `srcset` file. If the estimate is much smaller than the real display width, the image can look blurry; check it at common breakpoints.

subtopics.title: Choose art direction with picture
subtopics.explanation: `` lets the browser choose among sources using media conditions or supported formats. Use it for art direction when a crop should change on a small screen, not just when the file should be smaller. Include a final `` fallback with meaningful alternative text.

subtopics.title: Write useful alternative text
subtopics.explanation: Write `alt` text for the information an image adds to the page. A decorative image can use empty alt text so screen readers skip it. Responsive cropping and alternative text solve different problems: keep important details visible and provide a text equivalent when the image carries meaning.

subtopics.title: Balance image quality and transfer size
subtopics.explanation: Check image sharpness, file size, and layout on real target screens. A large source can waste mobile data, while an overly small source can look blurry on a high-density display. Reserve layout space with dimensions or `aspect-ratio` to avoid content jumping as the image loads.

foundations.overview: Responsive images give the browser several image choices. srcset lists candidates; sizes describes the rendered width; picture can select different crops or formats. This avoids downloading a huge image for a small screen while preserving image quality.
foundations.mentalModel: A shopkeeper offers the package size that fits the customer’s basket.
foundations.whyItMatters: Images are often a major part of page transfer size.

keyTakeaways: srcset lists width or density candidates.
sizes estimates the image’s display width.
picture supports art direction and format choices.
Measure bandwidth and visual quality on target screens.
